named_other_account_result.applied_fact: endpoint exact identity p_xy=1-(Q+R)/(2E); in the equal-predecessor branch the new deletion channels refine E-Q into positive first-successor channels and R into the dual negative-channel total

essential_step: For any incomparable equal-predecessor pair a,b, deleting a,b yields common-left insertion intervals of lengths r,s and exact fiber defect A_tau-B_tau=min(r,s)(s-r). The positive defect partitions over canonical first-successor Hasse blockers z of a, each channel lying inside the event a<z<b. In a width-at-most-three no-balanced candidate with a before b in the common strong-majority order, either one such blocker lies strictly between a and b in that order, giving a strictly shorter extreme incomparable span, or there are exactly two positive Hasse blockers after b and at least one channel has mass >E/6.
first_boundary_application: For the inherited first-boundary sibling blockers s1,s2, if no lower distinguisher exists then Pred(s1)=Pred(s2), so the theorem forces span descent or a second two-cover fork. In the second-fork case width three forces the original endpoint y to be poset-below at least one new blocker.
next_missing_step: Couple lower-distinguisher and span-descent/fork-escalation branches with delayed distinguishers plus the simultaneous >E/3 three-chain heavy slices and >E/81 central cells; prove finite escalation forces a balanced pair, a four-antichain, a proper autonomous nonchain, or a flux contradiction.
